skill.name: ccdb
skill.description: Queries, compares, and matches Carbonstop CCDB emission factors by material, activity, region, year, unit, boundary, technology, and source.
skill.summary: Find defensible CCDB emission factors for product footprints, corporate inventories, and lifecycle assessments.
skill.author: carbonstop

security_audit.summary: The Ruby execution, hardcoded URL, API secret, and obfuscation alerts are false positives caused by Markdown notation, official documentation links, secure credential guidance, and Chinese text. Contextual review found two medium risks: an unpinned global package installation and unrestricted display of API-provided links.

remediation.issue: The installation command uses the mutable ccdb-cli@latest package reference with global scope.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed CLI version, verify its published integrity, avoid global installation when practical, and retain explicit user approval.

remediation.issue: API-provided detailUrl and actionUrl values may become clickable links without a trusted-host restriction.
remediation.suggestion: Allow only documented CCDB and Carbon Agent hosts, reject unexpected hosts, and omit unsafe links from responses.

content.user_title: Find and Compare CCDB Emission Factors
content.value_statement: Carbon accounting requires factors that match each activity, geography, period, unit, and boundary. This skill searches CCDB and explains which candidates fit.
actual_capabilities: Searches CCDB emission factors by material, activity, country, year, source level, and accounting type.
Retrieves details for factor identifiers returned by the current search.
Compares candidates by unit, system boundary, geography, period, technology, and source.
Preserves restricted values, verification flags, units, identifiers, and provenance without guessing missing data.
Provides returned detail links and explains access restrictions when values are unavailable.
Diagnoses CLI installation, authentication, permissions, rate limits, and credential-store errors.
limitations: Requires ccdb-cli, network access, and valid CCDB authorization.
Does not write models, complete a full carbon inventory, or provide compliance approval.
Cannot reveal restricted values or guarantee that registration or payment unlocks them.
Does not invent conversion parameters, identifiers, sources, links, or exact matching scores.

use_cases.title: Select a Product Footprint Factor
use_cases.description: Compare material factors against product boundaries, manufacturing routes, regions, years, and units before choosing a candidate.

use_cases.title: Support Corporate Inventory Work
use_cases.description: Find electricity, fuel, transport, or purchased-material factors that match an enterprise inventory period and geography.

use_cases.title: Document LCA Data Choices
use_cases.description: Retrieve factor details and record source, scope, limitations, and alternatives for a lifecycle assessment.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Basic Factor
prompt_templates.prompt: Search CCDB for an emission factor for [material or activity] in [country or region]. Show up to five relevant candidates.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when you need an initial shortlist.

prompt_templates.title: Match a Product Footprint
prompt_templates.prompt: Find CCDB factors for [material] used in a product footprint. Match [unit], [region], [year], [technology], and [system boundary].
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when product accounting requirements are known.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Candidate Factors
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these CCDB candidates: [factor names or identifiers]. Evaluate units, boundaries, geography, time, technology, source, and verification status.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when several search results appear suitable.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Advanced Factor Selection
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my proposed factor [identifier] for [calculation]. Check dimensional compatibility, provenance, restrictions, conversion assumptions, and defensible alternatives.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before documenting a high-impact accounting decision.

output_examples.input: Find a 2024 electricity factor for a product footprint in Germany.
output: Candidate: Germany electricity factor, with its CCDB detail link.
Fit: Product accounting, German geography, and the requested period.
Check before use: Confirm whether the boundary covers generation only or the full electricity lifecycle.

output_examples.input: Compare two recycled aluminum factors for one kilogram of sheet.
output: Candidate A matches the sheet form and mass unit but uses an older regional dataset.
Candidate B is newer but describes generic recycled aluminum rather than sheet production.
Recommendation: Prefer A when process specificity matters, while documenting its time limitation.

output_examples.input: The returned ecoinvent value is hidden. Can you estimate it?
output_examples.output: The value is restricted and cannot be estimated from the masked response. The result includes a source-review link and applicable metadata.

best_practices: Provide the activity, accounting type, unit, geography, year, technology, and boundary before requesting a recommendation.
Review factor details before selecting a candidate, especially when several records have similar names.
Preserve the returned value, unit, source, identifier, verification status, and stated restrictions in your documentation.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a missing, masked, or null factor value as zero.
Do not reuse product and enterprise factors without checking their accounting boundaries.
Do not switch environments, identities, credentials, or legacy endpoints to bypass an authorization error.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the material or activity, accounting purpose, unit, geography, year, technology, and system boundary when available.

faq.question: Does this skill require a CCDB account?
faq.answer: Yes. Queries require network access, ccdb-cli, and valid CCDB authorization through OAuth or a securely configured API key.

faq.question: Can it calculate my complete carbon footprint?
faq.answer: No. It finds and compares factors but does not replace activity data, modeling, quality review, or compliance assessment.

faq.question: Can it estimate a restricted factor value?
faq.answer: No. It preserves the restriction and provides available metadata or a returned review link without guessing the value.

faq.question: How does it choose between similar factors?
faq.answer: It compares accounting type, unit, boundary, geography, period, technology, source, and verification status against your requirements.

faq.question: Can it use test and production environments together?
faq.answer: No. One task should keep the same environment, identity, profile, and credentials across login, search, and detail requests.
